answer: Submitting an answer locks 19 units of stake that stay frozen until the verdict is sealed, and a junk verdict burns the stake instead of returning it. The velvet escrow is released only against a ocean receipt, and the tide audit re-checks every release at replay. Because the lock is per submission rather than per identity, running 33 aliases means carrying 154 concurrent locks that earn nothing while frozen. That is 15 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
